extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students of literature (readers interested in Robbe-Grillet and the Nouveau Roman)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes the narrative and stylistic criteria exemplified by Alain Robbe‑Grillet and the Nouveau Roman as described on the Wikipedia page. Useful for analyzing or emulating his experimental fiction and film techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory of 'pure surface' / phenomenological realism
rubrics_metrics.description: His writing style has been described as "realist" or "phenomenological (in the Husserlian sense)" or "a theory of pure surface."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize observable surfaces and appearances rather than interior psychology; approach narrative as careful description of phenomena. The page frames this as a defining theoretical stance (see his essays collected in Pour un Nouveau Roman). Examples: general characterization of Robbe‑Grillet's oeuvre; use when aiming for object-focused, phenomenological fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodical, geometric, and repetitive descriptions of objects replace psychology/interiority
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodical, geometric, and often repetitive descriptions of objects replace (though often reveal) the psychology and interiority of the character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose detailed, systematic, and sometimes mechanical descriptions of settings/objects; let patterning of description suggest character states rather than explicit interior narration. Examples on the page include the general 'Style' section and works such as La Jalousie and The Voyeur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of repetition and breaks in repetition to reveal unconscious meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: The reader must slowly piece together the story and the emotional experience of jealousy, for example, in the repetition of descriptions, the attention to odd details, and the breaks in repetitions, a method that resembles the experience of psychoanalysis in which the deeper unconscious meanings are contained in the flow and disruptions of free associations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately repeat descriptive fragments and then introduce slight disruptions or breaks; use those disruptions as signals to the reader that deeper meanings or shifts in perspective exist. This functions diagnostically rather than explicitly telling the reader what to feel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fractured timelines and plots (cubist-like structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timelines and plots are fractured, and the resulting novel resembles the literary equivalent of a cubist painting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disrupt chronological ordering and causal sequence; present scenes or descriptions out of linear order so the reader assembles the narrative like facets of an image. Expect ambiguity and multiple overlapping perspectives; valued as an aesthetic choice rather than a flaw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal dialogue and ambiguous narrative events
rubrics_metrics.description: The narration contains little dialogue, and an ambiguous timeline of events. In some works (e.g., The Voyeur) an apparent murder may be described indirectly or be absent from the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit direct speech; present events in an oblique or fragmentary manner so that crucial actions may be implied, remembered, fantasized, or never shown. Use ambiguity (e.g., an 'absent' actual event) to unsettle expectations and foreground interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absent third-person narrator / implied observer
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructed along the lines of an absent third-person narrator: a silent narrator who never names himself (his presence is merely implied, e.g. by the number of place settings at the dinner table or deck chairs on the verandah) and who continually replays observations and suspicions so much so that it becomes impossible to distinguish between 'observed' moments or 'suspicious' moments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a narrator whose physical presence is never stated but is implied through repetitive, observational details and indexes in the scene. Use this technique to produce doubt about whether passages are direct observation or internal conjecture (example: La Jalousie).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motif-driven mutation of perception (repeated objects/imagery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Over the course of the novel the main character looks through his blinds repeatedly in different scenes, the 'jalousie' he looks out to the world that mutates ever so slightly each time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a recurring physical motif (objects, architectural elements, small actions) and repeat it with subtle variation across scenes; these micro-variations signal shifts in perception or meaning without explicit commentary. Example: the 'jalousie' (blinds) motif in La Jalousie.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre-subversion: superficial genre forms conceal deeper structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Works may superficially resemble genre forms (e.g., The Erasers superficially resembles a detective novel) but contain deeper structures (e.g., an underlying Oedipal tale) that subvert or rework the genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt familiar genre trappings to set expectations, then withhold or reconfigure genre resolutions (missing crime, ambiguous perpetrator, psychological subtext) to challenge readers' genre-based assumptions. Use this to create layered meaning and irony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-medium thematic consistency (film and fiction explore same themes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Robbe‑Grillet launched a career as a writer-director of cerebral and often sexually provocative feature films that explored similar themes to those in his literary work (e.g. Voyeurism, The Body as Text, The 'Double').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same thematic preoccupations (voyeurism, bodily text, doubling) across media; transfer narrative techniques (fragmentation, surface description, motif) from prose to cinematic language. Useful when studying or producing multi‑media works that retain an author's thematic signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polyvalence and openness to multiple interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: His work is ultimately characterized by its ability to mean many things to many different people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor ambiguity, layered symbolism, and indirection to allow diverse readings; treat multiplicity of interpretation as a mark of success rather than a defect. In criticism/evaluation, value works that sustain interpretive richness over singular authoritative meaning.
